population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: of the 18.8 on in 2030, 10.3 stayed on and 8.5 stopped; the off pool (7.7 + 8.5 = 16.2) restarted at 50% (8.1); 6.4 pts of new ever-users, of whom 4.8 are on and 1.6 already off; on = 10.3 + 8.1 + 4.8 = 23.2; off = (16.2 − 8.1) + 1.6 = 9.7 = 32.9 − 23.2; cycled = 8.9 prior cyclers + ~3.5 first-time restarts + ~0.3 new-cohort restarts = 12.7 of 32.9 ever-users ≈ 39%. Persistence improved slightly from 50% to 55% because the price steps down. Restarts stayed high because the 2×90-day cessation caps and the Medicaid waiver lockouts produce scheduled stops and restarts. Of ~270M adults, ~62.6M are current users. Age bands are weighted 20/33/24/23%: 2.6 + 8.25 + 8.88 + 3.45 = 23.2. The 65+ figure of 15% is ≈9.3M people. Income thirds: (29 + 23 + 17.6)/3 = 23.2. Bottom-third growth came through the HRSA expansion (Foundayo for vaping cessation through quitlines) and cheaper cash pills, and is mostly on liraglutide, rationed cessation courses or compounded product. Off-drug: ~26.2M adults have used and stopped (9.7%), many on a scheduled gap. ~181M have never used, a group that increasingly includes deliberate refusers since the reward-blunting label (Sep 2031). Pediatric: ~1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, of whom ~130k are aged 6–11 on liraglutide. Another ~60–90k 16–17-year-olds are estimated to take off-label or gray Foundayo for vaping, which is labelled for 18+ only. The first adolescent cohorts now have ~9 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: Structure unchanged. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was renewed again (Dec 2031) through 2033. Payment fell from $275 to $245 under the negotiated step-down; the $50 copay and the criteria are unchanged, and the DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+ is retained. Obesity Bridge users number ~2.8M: 2.8M × $245 × 12 ≈ $8.2B/yr. Medicare pays ≈15.7% of incretin users ≈ 9.8M (9.3M aged 65+ plus ~0.5M disabled). Medicaid pays ≈11% ≈ 6.9M at a $245 net: 6.9M × $245 × 12 ≈ $20.3B/yr combined federal and state. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program, FY2032 appropriation $5.8B (up from $4.5B): 2.6M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 ≈ $2.18B; 1.2M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $169 × 12 ≈ $2.43B; 0.6M Foundayo for smoking/vaping cessation through quitlines × $129 × 12 ≈ $0.93B; total ≈ $5.54B, with the remainder spent on site administration. Total ≈ 4.4M users.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India sells 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month and its first generic tirzepatide approvals launched in 2031 at $25–60. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide, and China has generic tirzepatide filings. In the US, ANDA filers hold tentative approvals for semaglutide. Patent settlements and device-patent litigation set US generic entry in 2033, so there is still no US generic.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~62.6M users: commercial 36.0% (22.5M), Medicare 15.7% (9.8M), Medicaid 11.0% (6.9M), HRSA free provision 7.0% (4.4M), cash/direct 15.0% (9.4M), gray 15.3% (9.6M) = 100%; 22.5 + 9.8 + 6.9 + 4.4 + 9.4 + 9.6 = 62.6M. The price decline came through negotiated channels: a Medicare negotiated price, the TrumpRx portal reset (Jun 2031) and PBM rebate deals made ahead of 2033 generic entry. Semaglutide injection cash fell from $349 to $249, tirzepatide from $449 to $299, and oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) from $199 to $149. Wegovy list is still $1,349. Retatrutide is still $1,499 list, allocated, with no portal price. Gray use grew in absolute terms (9.0M → 9.6M) but fell as a share (18% → 15.3%), because $149 pills undercut many 503A telehealth offers ($119–219). Indian mail pens ($6–40) and research retatrutide ($100–220) are unaffected. Coverage is still rationed: plans keep weight exclusions and pay through the cessation mandate, AUD parity and the CV/OSA/MASH/CKD labels.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
smoking and e-cigarette/vaping cessation, adults 18+ (orforglipron/Foundayo, Oct 2031)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: Foundayo for vaping cessation in 16–17-year-olds, through pediatricians or gray supply
'focus'/'quiet' low-dose oral subscriptions, now shrinking after the label and FTC consent orders (~1.1M users, down from 1.5–2M)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens with DEXA and strength coaching in the top income third
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
scheduled 'dose holidays' around weddings, holidays, pitches and performances, now routine and discussed in clinic
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market (driver: none). MariTide (BLA filed Jul 2030) received a major-amendment review extension over immunogenicity and device data, and then a CRL in Mar 2032 on manufacturing comparability; Amgen has resubmitted with a decision not before 2033. Survodutide's resubmission drew a second CRL in Nov 2031 over hepatic signals. Boehringer is running an additional safety study. Amycretin was resubmitted in Jun 2031 after Novo's North Carolina site was reinspected and received an FDA extension; its decision is due early 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3. The nicotine driver is realised as a supplement: orforglipron (Foundayo) sNDA for smoking and e-cigarette cessation (filed Nov 2030, approved Oct 2031). Semaglutide's cessation label was not extended to vaping. Market ≈$140B in 2032: US volume +25% offsets a ~20% net price decline. Lilly's revenue growth slowed after the scandal but the company kept volume leadership.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Higher among gray-market users and among cessation-course users who titrate quickly to fit a 90-day window.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation is still disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~61,000 filed and tolled claims. Two of three bellwethers have gone for plaintiffs, and global settlement talks opened in 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Reserves were raised at both manufacturers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; rising in absolute numbers with retatrutide and research-peptide use.
Still no causal confirmation and a low absolute risk. About 8,000 claims sit in the MDL, and litigation remains ahead of the science.
About 1.5× sarcopenia criteria in 65+ after more than 2 years. The 2032 NHANES release shows lean-mass index falling in low-income users while rising in high-income users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028) stands. Bridge counselling visit retained. HRSA added optional protein/strength handouts but no body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. First interim adolescent DEXA data (2032) show small BMD z-score lags that have not been interpreted. The 6–11 bone-accrual study has not reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. Pediatric bone-accrual studies ongoing; FDA advisory committee scheduled for 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the AUD and cessation populations.

The retatrutide postmarketing SHAPS study and pooled class analyses (2031) found reduced pleasure in ~9% of users on drug more than 12 months versus ~4% in matched non-users. Clinically significant anhedonia was ~2–3%, rising to ~5% at top retatrutide doses. The effect is dose-dependent and mostly reverses within 4–8 weeks of a dose reduction or stop.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling change (Sep 2031): a Warnings and Precautions section on 'reduced pleasure and emotional blunting' with prevalence figures and a recommendation to reassess dose. The Medication Guide was updated. FTC consent orders (2032) with five 'focus' telehealth brands bar mood claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven by structural stops (cessation course caps, waiver lockouts) and by voluntary stops after the anhedonia label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D and protein signals persist in older and low-income users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine of adolescent follow-up. ~130k children aged 6–11 are on drug. There is still no pubertal-timing data beyond trial length.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements and the pediatric registry continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls plateaued at their 2030 level as cheaper branded pills drew some users back. Research retatrutide purity problems persist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts continue. The first federal misbranding indictments were brought against two peptide vendors in 2032; individual users are still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; more often reported in research-peptide users.

safety_ledger.effect: Mood effects during nicotine withdrawal in young adult vapers
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Quitline programmes report that some 18–25-year-olds cannot tell withdrawal dysphoria from labelled reward blunting. Registry data are thin.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Foundayo cessation label requires mood check-ins at weeks 4 and 12. FDA has asked for an adolescent study before any under-18 label.

food_and_beverage.state: Snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes keep falling at about the 2028–30 rate. Lower prices are holding users on drug rather than recruiting many new ones. Majors finish divesting indulgent brands to private equity and discount specialists. Protein, fibre and bone-health formats grow. In high-HRSA zip codes, dollar-store baskets show smaller volumes without a protein shift.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer contract for a fourth year as AUD coverage matures. Premium single-serve and non-alcoholic lines grow. Vape makers report the steepest US decline in their history after Foundayo's cessation label and quitline distribution. Several states have revised their nicotine excise forecasts down 8–12%.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fine dining has adapted to small-plate tasting formats and 'holiday weekend' bookings timed to dose skips. Alcohol attach rates are still falling.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. The growth segment is athletic-cut tailoring, and the Dallas–Plano corporate corridor is now its second-biggest market after Charlotte. Plus-size continues to shrink; 'straight-size, low-muscle' fits sell at value retailers.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios keep expanding. Low-cost gyms gain subsidy users but churn them after cessation courses end. Research-peptide sales on gym floors are now an indictment risk.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend eases from ~+14% to ~+10% as net prices fall, but volume keeps rising through the cessation mandate, which now includes Foundayo for vaping. Employer weight-management coverage is 56%. Employers that subsidised 'focus' subscriptions as a perk mostly dropped them after the label on legal advice.

pharma.state: Lilly keeps volume leadership despite the scandal: shares fell ~18% on the unsealing, there is a DOJ civil investigation and shareholder suits, and growth slowed. Novo cut prices ahead of 2033 generic entry. HRSA liraglutide contract makers remain steady winners. Generic filers are waiting for 2033.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape is read as a payer statement. Lean and muscled with a known DEXA number means retatrutide, a coach and top-third money. Thin and soft means clinic liraglutide, a quitline pill or a compounded pen. Heavier means uninsured, between courses or a deliberate refuser. Since the label, 'refuser' has gained some prestige among the affluent.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class line is the finish, not the weight. In the Plano–Frisco corporate corridor in Texas, women aged 30–49 in relocated HQs wear 'the Legacy West look': retatrutide through concierge practices, Pilates-and-strength studios and published lean-mass percentages. The night cleaning and food-service staff in the same buildings are on HRSA liraglutide or quitline Foundayo with no body-composition monitoring. The 2032 NHANES release made the gap measurable: the income BMI gap narrowed while the lean-mass gap widened.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller meals are the default. Family tables with a child on liraglutide are common enough that school cafeterias offer 'half trays'. Celebrations are planned around dose holidays, and hosts ask guests whether they are 'skipping this week'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule and now often the dose band. 'Holiday-friendly' signals someone who takes breaks. Since the label, 'flat' has become a common reason given for breakups.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still clinical, but the label made wanting itself a measurable side effect. A craving is now either untreated or protected, depending on class and politics.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Sep 2031: ~9% reduced pleasure versus ~4% in matched non-users after 12 months, and 2–3% clinically significant, rising to ~5% at top retatrutide doses. Surveys find ~40% of long-term users have taken at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year, and ~15% have lowered their dose for mood reasons. 'Focus' subscriptions fell to ~1.1M users after the FTC consent orders, counted inside the cash and gray shares.
interior_life.framing: Treated as a side effect again, but an ordinary one you plan around. 'The grey' is the everyday term, 'holiday' is the fix, and clinicians document SHAPS scores the way they document BMI.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the label, most employers dropped 'focus' perks for liability reasons. Call-centre and logistics firms quietly kept some. Sales, creative and hospitality staff schedule holidays before pitches and peak seasons. Three more union contracts bar employer access to dose or adherence data. Trucking fleets still rely on tirzepatide for DOT apnea clearance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' has gone from a niche credit to a mainstream marketing line on festival bills, streaming comedy and novels. Critics complain the label is now meaningless. Sports betting handle stays soft in high-uptake states, with a small bump on holiday weekends that operators mention on earnings calls.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule dose holidays around anniversaries and conception attempts. Therapists use the label's prevalence figure in sessions. Partners on different doses negotiate holidays the way they once negotiated vacations.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The label and the Lilly hearings gave the 'pacification pills' critique of HRSA a factual hook. In the 2032 campaign, candidates of both parties are asked about the quitline Foundayo programme for young adults. A contested working paper claims a small turnout dip in high-uptake precincts, and nobody has replicated it. The appropriation still passed with bipartisan votes.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications (Foundayo for vaping cessation) and defensive on safety: the class anhedonia label, CRLs for MariTide and survodutide, an amycretin extension, and the first peptide-vendor indictments. The Lilly scandal led FDA to tighten its periodic safety-report review for incretins and to demand raw postmarketing datasets.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was renewed and expanded to $5.8B for FY2032 by a bipartisan rider. It adds Foundayo for smoking and vaping cessation through state quitlines, and many sites serve 18–25-year-olds. It remains discretionary and must be renewed annually. There is no mandate to take the drug. The Medicare Bridge was renewed at $245/$50. The ACA cessation mandate now covers Foundayo, and parity still covers semaglutide for AUD.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, 12-month lockout). Of the three states that applied, one (Oklahoma) was approved in 2031 with the same terms. HRSA sites still require only refill pickup, so the two-tier system persists. Quitline Foundayo adds mood check-ins, which are logged but not shared with payers.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening still drives tirzepatide use among drivers. The Army's recruit policy is unchanged and still contested. The VA and DoD adopted Foundayo for vaping cessation among service members in 2032, and DoD tracks anhedonia check-ins for aviation and weapons-qualified roles.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs stand, but negotiated price cuts eroded the brand premium. India's generic tirzepatide exports opened a new mail-order channel that trade negotiators now raise alongside semaglutide. Indian API still feeds US 503A compounders. The coming 2033 US generic entry has Indian and Israeli generic makers building US-facing fill-finish capacity.

events.event: Unsealed whistleblower suit in Indianapolis alleges Eli Lilly held back for 14 months an interim retatrutide postmarketing analysis showing dose-dependent anhedonia-scale shifts, and funded 'focus' telehealth affiliates through a speaker network. Lilly says the data were ambiguous. DOJ opens a civil investigation and Lilly shares fall 18%.

The TrumpRx portal reset and Medicare's negotiated price cut cash semaglutide to $249, tirzepatide to $299 and oral starting doses to $149. The Bridge and Medicaid net price falls to $245, as Novo and Lilly cut prices ahead of 2033 generic entry.

FDA adds a class Warnings and Precautions section for 'reduced pleasure and emotional blunting' to all incretin labels, citing ~9% prevalence after 12 months versus ~4% in matched non-users, and advises dose reassessment
FDA approves orforglipron (Foundayo) for smoking and e-cigarette cessation in adults, bringing the $149 pill under the ACA preventive mandate

Appropriations rider renews the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program at $5.8B for FY2032 and adds free Foundayo for vaping cessation through state quitlines. The Medicare Bridge is renewed through 2033 at $245 with a $50 copay.

CDC's first NHANES 2029–31 release shows the income gap in obesity prevalence narrowed by a third while the gap in lean-mass index between top and bottom income thirds widened, the first federal measurement of the 'class build'

open_tensions: US generic semaglutide enters in 2033 under patent settlements. Payers, HRSA and the Bridge set 2032 prices on brand terms, and it is unclear who captures the cliff, and whether the free programme shifts from liraglutide to generic semaglutide or is cut as 'no longer needed'.

Reward blunting is now a labelled harm with a prevalence number. Yet the state hands the same drug free to young vapers and heavy drinkers, and the public-health case for cessation runs straight into the 'pacification' critique in an election year.

The Lilly DOJ investigation and the MDL 3094 settlement talks are both open. A global settlement or a False Claims Act resolution could reshape labels, marketing rules and prices before the anhedonia and pancreatitis science settles.
Lean mass and bone now track income. The first adolescent DEXA lags and the unreported 6–11 bone-accrual study land on a subsidised population with no body-composition monitoring.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; entry is now set for 2033.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Now With a Prevalence Estimate: Sixty Million Americans, One New Label, and the Weekend Everyone Skips
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 a little under a quarter of American adults are taking an incretin drug, about sixty-two million people. Two years ago it was fifty million. The growth was quieter this time. Nothing new reached the market: MariTide drew a complete response letter, survodutide drew its second, and amycretin is still waiting on a reinspected plant. Prices fell instead. Novo and Lilly negotiated cuts ahead of generic semaglutide, which patent settlements have now set for 2033, and the portal reset in June 2031 took injected semaglutide to $249 a month, tirzepatide to $299 and the starter pills to $149. Wegovy still lists at $1,349. Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 and is still rationed. Who pays is unchanged. Employers that exclude weight loss still pay for quitting smoking and drinking less, and Medicare's Bridge still charges fifty dollars.

Smoking now includes vaping. In October 2031 the FDA approved Lilly's Foundayo pill for smoking and e-cigarette cessation. The preventive mandate made plans cover it, and the renewed federal programme, now $5.8 billion, began handing it out free through state quitlines. Many of the people who call are in their early twenties. Vape makers have reported their worst US year. The pill's label tells quitline nurses to ask about mood at week four and week twelve. Young adults often can't say whether they're feeling nicotine withdrawal or the other thing.

The other thing now has a number. In February 2031 a whistleblower suit unsealed in Indianapolis said Lilly had sat for fourteen months on a retatrutide analysis showing dose-dependent changes on an anhedonia scale, and had paid speakers tied to the 'focus' pill brands. Lilly said the data were ambiguous, and the Justice Department opened an investigation. Seven months later the FDA put a warning section on every incretin label: about nine percent of long-term users report reduced pleasure, against four percent of comparable non-users, and two to three percent meet the bar for clinically significant anhedonia. The effect fades within weeks of a dose cut. People already called it 'the grey', and since the label they plan around it. Four in ten long-term users took a deliberate dose holiday last year. Hosts ask wedding guests whether they're skipping that week. Restaurants fill on holiday weekends. Most employers that paid for 'focus' subscriptions dropped them once their lawyers read the label.

The bodies tell the rest. In May the CDC published the first national survey data of the drug era. The income gap in obesity has narrowed by a third, while the gap in lean muscle mass between the richest and poorest thirds has grown. In the corporate campuses of Plano and Frisco, the women who run divisions get retatrutide through concierge practices and post their lean-mass percentages. The women who clean their offices at night take clinic liraglutide or a quitline pill and are not offered a scan. Both groups are thinner than their mothers. Only one is stronger. The first adolescent bone scans show small lags that nobody has interpreted yet, and the study of six-to-eleven-year-olds hasn't reported.

The sixty-one thousand claims in the Philadelphia courtroom are moving toward settlement. Spirits are down for a fourth year, and snack brands keep moving into private-equity portfolios. Indiana's weigh-in kiosks still decide who keeps Medicaid, and Oklahoma has added its own. In the campaign, candidates are asked whether giving young people a free pill that can dull pleasure is public health or pacification. Both parties voted to fund it. From the outside the country looks calmer, leaner and mostly smoke-free. Up close, you can see who paid for the drug in how much muscle a body has.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Treviño, twenty-four, wakes at three in the afternoon in Garland and takes the small white Foundayo tablet with tap water. It's day sixty-one of her second ninety-day course, and the quitline paid for both. Her vape sits in a kitchen drawer under the takeout menus, its battery dead since August.

The nurse calls at four for the week-eight check-in. Marisol rates her pleasure from one to five and says three, because she isn't sure what four used to feel like. The nurse types it and says it's in range.

At nine she badges into a tower at Legacy West and pushes a cart through a floor of standing desks. A woman from finance is still there at ten, eating six almonds from a jar. She has shoulders like a swimmer, and there's a printout of a body scan pinned to her cubicle wall, with a percentage circled in green. Marisol wipes the glass beside it.

On her break she texts her mother, who picks up liraglutide every month at the clinic on Jupiter Road and has stopped making tamales because nobody eats more than one. Her cousin Danny's quinceañera for his daughter is Saturday. Marisol texts back: skipping Friday.

At two a.m. she vacuums an empty boardroom. A screen on the wall loops a recruiting video full of people who look like the woman with the almonds. She doesn't want the vape. She doesn't especially want anything. It's quiet in her head.

At six she drives home past the 7-Eleven without stopping and decides that counts as a good night.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CDC's first NHANES 2029–31 release shows the income gap in obesity prevalence narrowed by a third
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a national survey with body-composition data released in May 2032, months after the 2029–31 fieldwork, is much faster than NHANES normally reports. A one-third narrowing of the income obesity gap is also asserted with no chain, when bottom-third users are mostly on low-efficacy or unverified product.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The nurse calls at four for the week-eight check-in.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world's own Foundayo cessation label requires mood check-ins at weeks 4 and 12, not week 8. It is also day sixty-one, which is week nine, so the prose contradicts the world state.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Market ≈$140B in 2032: US volume +25% offsets a ~20% net price decline.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 1.25 × 0.8 = 1.0, so US revenue is flat. With ex-US generic erosion continuing, the market should not rise from about $135B to $140B. This also sits badly with pharmacy trend easing only to +10% and with Lilly's growth slowing.

rationale.badness: Inequality is the worst dimension (7). Lean mass and bone now track income (NHANES event, safety ledger), a subsidised population gets no body-composition monitoring, and 16–17-year-olds are using gray Foundayo with unreported adolescent bone data. Flourishing and cohesion are worse than 2030 through reward blunting, 'flat' as a breakup reason, and dose-holiday-driven social planning. Epistemic harm is lower (4) because the label and SHAPS scores make the harm nameable and measured. The overall 5.5 is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events. Adoption is +4.4 exactly, managed decline is the 2031 portal reset, the anhedonia label is Sep 2031, the Lilly scandal is Feb 2031, nicotine is realised as a Foundayo sNDA, and the subsidy is the $5.8B HRSA rider. Nothing contradicts a driver. mechanism: most changes have chains, such as price cuts driving persistence, cessation caps driving cycling, and the scandal leading to the label, the employer perk drop and the FTC orders. Weak points are the rushed NHANES release and unexplained obesity-gap narrowing (claim 1), persistence rising despite voluntary stops after the label, and the prose week-8 check-in contradicting the label's weeks 4 and 12 (claim 2). magnitude: on-drug 23.2, ever-used 32.9, the income thirds and the age bands all sit inside the envelope and reconcile. The payer mix, the Bridge, Medicaid and HRSA arithmetic, and the user counts also multiply out. The only gap is the market-size arithmetic (claim 3).
rationale.generativity: The Marisol Treviño day-in-the-life shows rather than explains: the nurse's pleasure rating, the dead vape, the almond-eating finance woman with the circled body scan, her mother no longer making tamales, and 'skipping Friday'. The world has many implied scenes, including the half-tray cafeteria, dose-holiday weddings and Legacy West versus the night cleaners. A few passages stay at the level of policy summary.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CDC's first NHANES 2029–31 release shows the income gap in obesity prevalence narrowed by a third while the gap in lean-mass index between top and bottom income thirds widened
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a national survey with DXA-derived lean-mass data covering 2029–31 is released in May 2032, and it already shows a one-third narrowing of the income gap in obesity. Survey release lags and a two-year effect size make this fast and convenient, and no chain is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Persistence improved slightly from 50% to 55% because the price steps down.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world also reports a September 2031 anhedonia label, 'voluntary stops after the anhedonia label', and about 40% of long-term users taking dose holidays. A roughly 25% price cut is asserted as the cause of better persistence while the countervailing forces are ignored.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Market ≈$140B in 2032: US volume +25% offsets a ~20% net price decline.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 1.25 × 0.8 leaves US revenue flat, and ex-US generic erosion continues (India and China, generic tirzepatide in India from 2031). The global market should fall from $135B, not rise to $140B.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder version of 2030 with new losers. Lean mass and bone now track income (NHANES event, lean-mass ledger entry), about 800k minors are on drug including 60–90k 16–17-year-olds on off-label or gray Foundayo for vaping, and a subsidised low-income population gets no body-composition monitoring. Coercive conditioning persists (Indiana, Arkansas and Oklahoma weigh-in kiosks), and reward blunting is a mainstream complaint managed with dose holidays. Epistemic harm is lower than in 2030 because anhedonia is now measured and labelled, so the overall score is about 5.5 rather than higher.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised in events and fields. Adoption lands at 23.2%, price_path shows a managed decline to $249/$299/$149, nicotine comes through an orforglipron sNDA, and anhedonia is labelled in Sep 2031. The scandal (Lilly whistleblower suit), subsidy (HRSA to $5.8B), class stratification, status-quo coverage, no next-gen launch and the mainstream-complaint personality layer are all present and consistent. mechanism: the chains for the price cuts, the scandal-to-label sequence and the Foundayo expansion are shown. Weak points are the fast NHANES release with lean-mass data, the persistence-because-of-price assertion, and the prose 'week-eight check-in' contradicting the label's week 4 and 12 check-ins. magnitude: all figures sit inside the envelope (23.2 on, 32.9 ever, bottom third 17.6 ≤ 23.2 ≤ top 29), no generic arrives and the Foundayo approval is a supplement to a marketed drug. The population arithmetic, payer mix (sums to 62.6M), Bridge, Medicaid and HRSA dollar figures all multiply out. The only gap is the market-size sentence, where flat US revenue plus ex-US erosion cannot produce $140B.
rationale.generativity: The prose has a vivid day in the life of Marisol, covering the quitline nurse's mood rating, the finance woman with the almonds and body-scan printout, her mother who has stopped making tamales, and the 'skipping Friday' text. The world fields supply many scene seeds: half trays, 'holiday weekend' bookings, dating-profile dose bands, and the Plano–Frisco 'Legacy West look'. The class contrast is shown rather than explained, so there is a great deal of usable film.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Vape makers report the steepest US decline in their history after Foundayo's cessation label and quitline distribution.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: only ~0.6M free Foundayo users exist 14 months after approval, which is too few to drive a record industry decline or 8–12% cuts to state excise forecasts. No chain through the wider nicotine-user base is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Persistence improved slightly from 50% to 55% because the price steps down.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the price cuts only began in Jun 2031, and the same world says the Sep 2031 label prompted voluntary stops and dose reductions. The claimed rise in persistence is asserted against the world's own pressures toward stopping.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Market ≈$140B in 2032: US volume +25% offsets a ~20% net price decline.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 1.25 × 0.8 = 1.0, so US revenue is flat. The parent said ex-US generic erosion was already being offset, and it continues, so a rise from $135B to $140B does not reconcile.

rationale.badness: Stratification deepens: lean mass and bone track income (NHANES, events 2032-05), and a subsidised population is left without body-composition monitoring. Children aged 6–11 and adolescents on drug have no bone data, and free Foundayo goes to young vapers with logged mood check-ins. The anhedonia harm is now labelled, measured and discussable, which lowers epistemic badness compared with 2030. The world is harder but not catastrophic, and the main losers are the poor, the young and older women with bone risk.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CDC's first NHANES 2029–31 release shows the income gap in obesity prevalence narrowed by a third
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a national survey with body-composition data released in May 2032, months after the 2029–31 fieldwork, is much faster than NHANES normally reports. A one-third narrowing of the income obesity gap is also asserted with no chain, when bottom-third users are mostly on low-efficacy or unverified product.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The nurse calls at four for the week-eight check-in.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world's own Foundayo cessation label requires mood check-ins at weeks 4 and 12, not week 8. It is also day sixty-one, which is week nine, so the prose contradicts the world state.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Market ≈$140B in 2032: US volume +25% offsets a ~20% net price decline.

rationale.badness: Inequality is the worst dimension (7). Lean mass and bone now track income (NHANES event, safety ledger), a subsidised population gets no body-composition monitoring, and 16–17-year-olds are using gray Foundayo with unreported adolescent bone data. Flourishing and cohesion are worse than 2030 through reward blunting, 'flat' as a breakup reason, and dose-holiday-driven social planning. Epistemic harm is lower (4) because the label and SHAPS scores make the harm nameable and measured. The overall 5.5 is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.
